<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via DuplicateRecordError (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-chatbot.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of class DuplicateRecordError))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of class DuplicateRecordError))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via describeEffectiveAccess (sdk, the bare tail of client method security.describeEffectiveAccess, bound to GET /api/v1/security/users/:id/effective-access))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`  _(via DuplicateRecordError (symbol, a top-level class), userMessage (symbol, a field of class DuplicateRecordError))_
- `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of class DuplicateRecordError))_
- `content/docs/ui/views.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of class DuplicateRecordError))_

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of class DuplicateRecordError))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of class DuplicateRecordError))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/index.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of class DuplicateRecordError))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of class DuplicateRecordError))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via describeEffectiveAccess (sdk, the bare tail of client method security.describeEffectiveAccess, bound to GET /api/v1/security/users/:id/effective-access))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7d06248d923d21d9cc453442ca89c324bd0304c0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c8558dddc2774d8092e235d3f75e79bbed37bc8f` — the merge of head `4e1aa4a2cc4f19eb787add2c0387128b7522ca95` into base `7d06248d923d21d9cc453442ca89c324bd0304c0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c8558dddc2774d8092e235d3f75e79bbed37bc8f && git checkout c8558dddc2774d8092e235d3f75e79bbed37bc8f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7d06248d923d21d9cc453442ca89c324bd0304c0 4e1aa4a2cc4f19eb787add2c0387128b7522ca95 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7d06248d923d21d9cc453442ca89c324bd0304c0 && git merge --no-ff 4e1aa4a2cc4f19eb787add2c0387128b7522ca95

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7d06248d923d21d9cc453442ca89c324bd0304c0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7d06248d923d21d9cc453442ca89c324bd0304c0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `099761b688156223ad7465c99ff32dc823de0927`
Local-runs: none

The face is the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` declaration alone: no published schema, no governed path and no narrowing in the diff (`packages/objectql`, `packages/metadata-protocol`, and test files in `rest`, `runtime`, `service-automation`, `verify`). Inputs: card #33790, the PR body, the net diff against merge base `021abd44`, and the head's check-runs.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The widening is a key the contract already declares: right.** `ApiErrorSchema.userMessage` (`packages/spec/src/api/contract.zod.ts`) is the producer-marked end-user channel, and `withDeclaredUserMessage` already rides it onto every classified `/data` body. No spec, schema or wire vocabulary moves; the duplicate refusal starts using a channel that exists.
- **What gains the key: right and bounded.** The engine's `DuplicateRecordError` declares `userMessage` equal to its `endUserMessage`, which was already the `/data` 409's `error` text. So every door that forwards a declared `userMessage` (the action door, the sandbox hand-back, the Hono seam, MCP tool errors, a flow's inner refusal) carries the writer's-locale sentence, and `message` stays the diagnostic. The text is not new: it names field labels only and quotes no record value, exactly what `error` already showed on the 409.
- **Row errors: right.** `toRowApiError` reads the one presence rule (`declaredUserMessage`) and the same bound (`boundedDeclaredUserMessage`, `truncateClientMessage`) the whole-request door applies, so a row now answers what the same throw answers on a single write. An unmarked throw adds no key (CONTROL pin). `message`, `code`, `httpStatus` and `details` are computed as before.
- **Unchanged keys: right.** `error`, `code`, `field` and `developerMessage` on the flat 409, and `message` on every door, keep their text; the flipped pins assert both halves (the new key, and the old keys unchanged).
- **The reversal of the module note is ruled.** The old docblock said that joining the `userMessage` channel was "a contract decision this sentence does not make". Seat ruling B′ (record 6895764754), on maintainer ruling C (record 6819749037), makes it, and the PR cites both.

### ② Semver level

`Metadata-protocol: none` holds: nothing a metadata author writes changes. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` holds: a consumer gains an optional key it may read and loses nothing. A non-protocol change takes `patch`; the changeset gives `patch` to `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, the two packages whose source moves. Match, and `Check Changeset` is green. No migration entry and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed (not breaking). No `Skills-docs:` line is owed (kind `none`, no narrowing arm).

### ③ Boundary flags

- A client that treats an exact-shape row or 409 body as closed sees one more key. In this repo, seven exact-shape pins in `packages/rest` were updated in the diff for that reason. The Console is not in the diff; that its action and bulk-edit surfaces render `userMessage` is the card's premise, not re-measured in this record.
- Import rows are declared unchanged (the row adopts the `/data` verdict's `error`, already localized); no pin, which is acceptable because no code moved there.
- Nothing is out of scope or owed elsewhere.

This is the B′ shape (seat record 6895764754 on maintainer ruling C, 6819749037): end-user text composed where it is produced.
- **The row carrier uses the one read and the one bound.** `toRowApiError` adds `boundedDeclaredUserMessage(err)`, the same `declaredUserMessage` presence rule and `truncateClientMessage` bound that `withDeclaredUserMessage` applies to whole-request bodies. A blank or non-string `userMessage` is no declaration, and an unmarked throw adds no key (CONTROL pin). The row's `code`, `message`, `httpStatus` and `details` are computed exactly as before.

- **Pins and ablations.** The new runtime file drives every door on a real kernel under `zh-CN` and `en`. The body's ablations are tight: the producer line removed reds 19 of 20 (the control stays green), and the row spread removed reds exactly the 8 row cases. The old `not.toHaveProperty('userMessage')` pins are flipped under claim amendment 6907854103, and each flipped pin also asserts the unchanged half (`message` and `error` keep their text).
- **Declarations.** `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none` and `patch` on both moved packages hold; see the TIER_DEFAULT record, comment 6909868878.

None.

1. `DuplicateRecordError` now holds the same string in `endUserMessage` and `userMessage`. That is fine as written. A later cleanup could make `endUserMessage` a getter over `userMessage`, so the two cannot drift if someone edits one assignment.
2. Import rows are declared unchanged with no pin. That is acceptable because no import code moved, but a one-line assertion in the card file would stop a future import-runner change from silently diverging.

55 check runs at this head (latest run of each): every one is success or skipped, none failed or pending. Test Core 1–8/8, Build Core, TypeScript Type Check, Lint & Repo Gates, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Live E2E UI, Check Changeset and the PR-body guards are success. The skips are the ui, docs, dogfood-shard and temporal jobs the path filter leaves out, the opt-in jobs, the queue-only and schedule-only verdicts, and a re-triggered Auto Label and Check PR Size whose earlier runs are success. The PR body records 69 of 71 derived dispatch gates run locally, all exit 0, with the remaining two green in CI.


> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；
> **断言**（`AssertionError: …`）才指向真实的行为改变。两者的 `FAIL` 行长得一模一样，只有这一行能区分。
>
> ⚠️ **断言这一侧有一类例外，判据是断言在测什么，不是它是不是 `AssertionError`。** 断言的对象是**产品行为**（一个值、一个形状、一次拒收）⇒ 照上面读：真实的行为改变，去查，⛔ 不要重排掉；
> 断言的对象是**这次实验自身的有效性前提**（跑完的耗时、负载下的先后、任何只在时间预算内才成立的条件）⇒ 它跟**超时**是同一类，同样对负载敏感，重排一次是合法的判别手段。
> 识别是机械的：断言的消息或它比较的值本身点名了一段**时长、一个时间戳、一个耗时计数**。实测过的一对 —— `AssertionError: SecurityPlugin.init() ran: expected false to be true` 测的是产品行为（真回归）；

> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）
